subject: PrivStack module carveout, egress policy matrix & CI/CD sanity checks
messages:
From: Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@acmecloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivStack carveout + egress constraints for on-prem rollout

Hi Mina / Grace,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. We have a target date for the on-prem rollout of the PrivStack for the first ACME internal tenant (pilot): July 12. Before we lock the date we need to validate a few infra items so our security & ops teams can sign off:

- Module carveout: we want each Redwood module (serving, routing, kv-cache, metrics) to be delivered as an isolated Helm+Terraform module so we can pin and roll individually. Attached is a high-level diagram showing desired carveouts.
- Egress policy matrix: ACME requires strict egress allow-lists by namespace and host. I've attached an initial matrix with expected IP ranges and DNS names.
- CI/CD sanity: We need a short checklist that the GitOps/CI pipeline will run (unit terraform plan checks, helm template lint, ansible idempotence checks, and OPA gating for egress).

Can you confirm: (1) which Redwood modules will be first to ship as carveouts, (2) who owns the Ansible hardening templates (ansible ownership), and (3) if we can add an automated OPA policy test into your GitLab pipeline for the egress matrix?

Attached: arch/privstack-module-carveout-diagram.svg, policy/egress-policy-matrix.xlsx

Appreciate the turnaround — ACME security needs this week to keep our July date.

--
Carlos Gomez
Senior Cloud Architect, ACME Cloud
carlos.gomez@acmecloud.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Gomez <carlos.gomez@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivStack carveout + egress constraints for on-prem rollout

Carlos — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, very helpful. Quick answers up front, then small plan:

1) First carveout modules: serving-runtime, kv-cache, and ingress-router. We propose shipping metrics/observability as a separate optional module in phase 2 to avoid cross-team rollout coupling.

2) Ansible ownership: infra-automation (that's me + Grace) will own the base hardening playbooks. Marcus will own network-level firewall templates and tftp/provisioning flow. We'll publish a short OWNERS.md in the repo and link it to your procurement checklist.

3) OPA gating: yes — we can add an OPA test that validates egress against the matrix as part of the merge pipeline. We'll stub a policy against the columns in your sheet and run it in the CI pre-merge step.

Plan (next 72 hours):
- Grace: draft ansible hardening patch + example helm values per carveout module (target Tue EOD).
- Marcus: provide firewall rule templates and the required cluster egress ACL snippets (target Tue EOD).
- Mina: create a CI checklist doc and a proposed GitLab job that runs terraform plan (with diff suppression for secret placeholders), helm template, ansible --check, and opa test (target Wed AM).

I'll attach the initial task breakdown and point people at the drive link. If ACME can confirm the IP ranges in the egress sheet by EOD Tue, we can lock the OPA policy tests.

Subject: Re: PrivStack carveout + egress constraints for on-prem rollout

Mina / all — I pushed a quick patch with an Ansible playbook skeleton and notes about where to split roles for the carveout (see attached). Key technical notes from our POV:

- Service mesh boundaries: the serving-runtime will be in its own namespace but still rely on the cluster mesh for mTLS. We need to validate that the mesh sidecar egress won't bypass namespace-level egress policies — on some vendor CNI+service-mesh combos the iptables ordering causes unintended egress.
- Helm value overrides: we'll introduce a top-level values-override per module (values.serving.carveout.enabled = true) to keep the upstream chart backward compatible.
- Ansible idempotence: the playbook uses a tagging strategy so the hardening step is re-runnable in staging. I'll include an --check job in the pipeline.
- OPA policies: I recommend expressing rules as small JSON arrays (allow-lists by namespace -> host) so the OPA tests are straightforward.

Attachments: patches/ansible-playbook-carveout.diff

Quick addition from networking:

- I'll produce firewall rule templates that follow ACME's canonical zones (mgmt, app, infra) and include an example iptables/nftables snippet for the provisioning VLAN.
- Two constraints: if ACME requires DNS-level allowlists (FQDN only) we need a sidecar DNS proxy in-phase 1 to avoid relying on cloud resolver features. If ACME supplies IP ranges, easier.
- For the GitLab gate: add an integration test that deploys helm templates into a small k3s staging cluster (ephemeral) and runs connectivity checks against the egress hosts listed. This is lightweight and catches obvious breakage.

I put the firewall templates and a sample GitLab job in the Drive link (JIRA-PRIV-4821). I'll coordinate with Ops to run a smoke verification next week.
